reliability_binding.label: A1
reliability_binding.chronology: Imported preexisting per-answer snapshot; original stop/seal times unavailable.

items.representation: CoeffMatrix I := I→I→ENNReal is input-first. IsLipOn requires U⊆dom φ and ∀x,y∈U,∀j, d j(φx)(φy)≤∑i L i j*d i x y. LipFamily is the legal certificate set; LipFamilyFull uses U=dom φ. I is finite and nonempty; all coefficients and distances are ENNReal.

IsCoLipOn requires U.Nonempty, U⊆dom φ, and ∀x,y∈U,∀j, ∑i K i j*d i x y≤d j(φx)(φy). CoLipFamily is the legal lower-bound certificate set. Coefficients are arbitrary ENNReal values, so 0 and ∞ are allowed.

Storage M i j is input i to output j. matMul M2 M1 i j=∑k M2 k j*M1 i k. toOrdinaryMatrix places output j as row and input i as column; toOrdinaryMatrix_apply records row j,column i=M i j, and toOrdinaryMatrix_matMul proves ordinary matrix multiplication gives the chapter composite.

matId is δij with both unit laws. matProd 0=M identity, matProd(n+1) M=matMul(M last)(matProd n prefix), matProd_one gives the unique one-step matrix. opProd is the parallel ordered operator product with identity at zero and last operator on the left at a successor, matching Lk...L1.

stepInput recursively defines U0=U and U(m+1)=φm(Um). stepInput_eq_opProd_image identifies Um with the prefix-composite image; stepInput_subset_dom_of_chain_dom proves Um⊆dom φm from U1⊆dom ck. lip_fin_chain builds the composite certificate only from step certificates on the actual input domains.

A complete path is k:Fin(n+1)→I with k0=i, k(last)=j, so all intermediate sequences are quantified. pathEdge M k m=M m(k m)(k(m+1)) with no positivity restriction. PathHasZero says every complete path has a zero edge; PathAllPositive says some complete path has all edges positive. The n=1 lemmas reduce to the unique empty intermediate sequence and M 0 i j.

Channel=I×I. RowSupport L i j means ∀k≠i,L k j=0 and RowDecoupled L j means ∃i,RowSupport L i j. ColumnSupport L i j means ∀k≠j,L i k=0 and ColumnDecoupled L i means ∃j,ColumnSupport L i j. IsDiagonal means ∀i≠j,L i j=0; CompletelyDecoupled names this diagonal certificate.

ScalarFeasible d φ U i j={lam:ENNReal | ∀x,y∈U, d j(φx)(φy)≤lam*d i x y}; U⊆dom φ is an ambient side condition of channel statements. singleChannelLipConstant is sInf of that set, so the empty infimum is ∞. It is not identified with a matrix entry.
For [Unique I], any L∈LipFamily d φ U satisfies d j(φx)(φy)≤L j j*d j x y for x,y∈U: the finite sum collapses to its unique term.
If U⊆dom φ, then LipFamilyFull d φ⊆LipFamily d φ U: full-domain Lip certificates restrict to U.
If U⊆V, then LipFamily d φ V⊆LipFamily d φ U: shrinking the evaluation domain enlarges the legal certificate family.
lipEntryInf d φ U i j=sInf{(L i j)|L∈LipFamily d φ U}. For U⊆V, lipEntryInf U i j≤lipEntryInf V i j.

If U1⊆dom(φ2∘φ1), L1 is legal for φ1 on U1 and L2 is legal for φ2 on the actual image φ1(U1), then matMul L2 L1 is legal for φ2∘φ1 on U1. The proof applies the two pointwise Lip inequalities and swaps finite sums.
If x,y∈dom φ, d j(φx)(φy)=0 and d i x y>0, then every global co-Lip K has K i j=0. This uses co-Lip lower boundedness, nonnegativity, and positivity of d i x y.
With U2=φ1(U1), legal K1 and K2 give matMul K2 K1 legal for φ2∘φ1 on the nonempty U1; nonemptiness comes from K1.
PointwisePerturbation records U⊆dom φ1∩dom φ2 and ∀z∈U,∀j,d j(φ1z)(φ2z)≤δj. perturbation_forward proves d j(φ2x)(φ2y)≤d j(φ1x)(φ1y)+δj+δj for x,y∈U.
Under the same perturbation hypotheses, d j(φ1x)(φ1y)≤d j(φ2x)(φ2y)+δj+δj, by swapping φ1,φ2 in P08 and using symmetry.
If also L∈LipFamily d φ1 U, then d j(φ2x)(φ2y)≤(∑i L i j*d i x y)+δj+δj for x,y∈U.
If also K∈CoLipFamily d φ1 U, then (∑i K i j*d i x y)≤d j(φ2x)(φ2y)+δj+δj.
For any length n, if every step L m is Lip on the actual domain stepInput φ U m, then matProd n L is Lip for opProd n φ on U. Only single-step certificates are assumed, not a final composite bound.
colip_fin_chain gives the finite co-Lip product with nonempty U; colip_fin_chain_positive treats n≥1 and obtains nonemptiness from the first co-Lip step. It uses the same actual image domains as P12.
For any U⊆dom(id_X), matId is legal Lip for opId on U, formalizing c0=id_X with empty matrix product matId.
For nonempty U⊆dom(id_X), the same matId is legal co-Lip for opId on U, including U.Nonempty.

For n≥1, (matProd n M)i j=0 iff every complete path from i to j has some zero layer entry. pathHasZero_one is the n=1 reduction; matProd_path_criteria proves zero and positive criteria simultaneously.
For n≥1, 0<(matProd n M)i j iff some complete path from i to j has all layer entries strictly positive. At n=1 this is the unique empty sequence and M 0 i j>0.
If x,y∈U, d i x y=0 and 0<d j(φx)(φy), every scalar candidate gives output≤lam*0=0, so ScalarFeasible is empty and its infimum is ∞.
If a is the single-channel infimum, 0<a<∞, then a∈ScalarFeasible; the full pointwise scalar inequality holds at a. The proof constructs strict finite candidates above a and uses upward closure.
If lam0 is feasible and lam0≤lam1, then lam1 is feasible; the feasible scalar family is upward closed.
If a is the infimum, a<∞ and a<lam (including lam=∞), then lam is feasible. This covers the positive finite-infimum context and is slightly stronger.
If the infimum is 0, every lam with 0<lam<∞ is feasible. It does not claim that 0 itself is feasible.

On Fin 3 with bot=0, counterD is 0 on the diagonal and ∞ off it, and counterGauge proves all extended-pseudometric axioms. counterOp is the identity, counterU={1,2} is nonempty and lies in dom(identity). The feasible scalars are exactly {lam|0<lam}; the infimum is 0 but 0 is not feasible.
For a=the single-channel infimum, a<∞ iff there is some lam<∞ in ScalarFeasible. The forward direction uses a+1 and P21; the reverse uses sInf≤lam.
If L i j=0, the term L i j*d i x y is 0 with no finiteness restriction on d i x y, and the output sum equals the same sum over univ\{i}; the input-i term is removed.
If L∈LipFamily and RowSupport L i j, then d j(φx)(φy)≤L i j*d i x y for x,y∈U; the unique input i need not equal j.
If ColumnSupport L i j, then every k≠j satisfies L i k*d i x y=0; in this upper-bound certificate input i contributes only to output j.
A diagonal L∈LipFamily gives, for every j and x,y∈U, d j(φx)(φy)≤L j j*d j x y; this is the row-support theorem with i=j.
For L∈LipFamily and K∈CoLipFamily on the same U, the sole row hypothesis ∀k≠j,L k j=0 yields K j j*d j x y≤d j(φx)(φy)≤L j j*d j x y. No analogous sparsity is required of K.

If the P29 Lip diagonal-row condition holds for all j, all componentwise two-sided bounds hold. The finite version additionally assumes L j j<∞ and K j j<∞ and returns the bounds together with those finiteness assertions.
If K∈CoLipFamily and K i j>0, then x,y∈U and d i x y>0 imply d j(φx)(φy)>0; the co-Lip sum is lower-bounded by the positive term K i j*d i x y.

GaugeZero means ∀i,d i x y=0 and gaugeZero_iff_gaugeZeroRelated identifies it with the frozen Chapter 1 relation. If K is co-Lip and every diagonal K j j>0, then GaugeZero d(φx)(φy) implies GaugeZero d x y for x,y∈U, using P31 componentwise.
